llm.summary: This is a legitimate browser automation skill, but it needs Review because its custom-code feature can exceed the documented sandbox while controlling an authenticated browser session.

dimensions.detail: A long-running localhost daemon controlling a visible browser is purpose-aligned, but it handles high-impact browser state and the token file permissions are not explicitly restricted despite documentation saying it is local-user-only.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is conventional for a Node skill: package.json declares only the playwright dependency and no package scripts were present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions repeatedly warn to use code execution only for trusted, user-directed tasks, but they also present broad arbitrary Playwright code patterns for form submission, page mutation, downloads, and save/publish workflows without a default least-privilege mode.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon persists across commands, stores an auth token under ~/.pw-browser/daemon.json, keeps browser session state alive, and enables eval/run-code unless safe mode is explicitly selected.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser automation purpose is coherent and the skill openly discloses eval, run-code, persistent browser state, cookie/storage access, downloads, and credentialed browser actions; the concern is that run-code is documented as unable to access Node/system APIs while the implementation uses Node vm with host objects, which is not a reliable security boundary.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the agents and pages that will use it. Prefer starting the daemon with PW_BROWSER_SAFE_MODE=1 unless arbitrary eval/run-code is truly needed, do not run untrusted code snippets, avoid sensitive logged-in sites during automation, and close the daemon when finished.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The high-risk browser and code-execution capabilities are expected for this skill and are disclosed in SKILL.md, including allowed Bash access and safe-mode guidance; this finding is not enough by itself, but it contributes to Review because the privileged surface is broad.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: pw-browser.js executes run-code through Node vm while exposing host objects such as the Playwright page, so the artifact-backed security boundary is weaker than the documentation claim that fs/process/require access is unavailable.
[SDI-4] expected: Partially accepted: browser-triggered downloads are expected for Playwright automation and are disclosed, but the docs should more clearly distinguish indirect local file writes and path/overwrite risk from the claim that run-code cannot write arbitrary files.
